tier_reason: Tier C stands; the decode part of the claim is dropped on the author's own correction (wavey-ai/soundkit, soundkit-opus/performance-results/2026-08-24-native-48k/README.md, 2026-08-25): the 1.50-4.64% decode lead timed each decoder on its own encoder's packets, and the same-packet i24 192 kb/s re-test gives +0.51% on C packets, -0.30% on Rust packets and +0.10% combined, which is parity. The remaining 1.19-2.36% encode lead is within the work asymmetry the enricher found (the analysis port skips libopus's MLP/GRU classifier; i16 decode hard-clamps where C opus_decode soft-clips) and the identity checksum covers only packet length plus first and last byte; decode drift between checkpoints with no decoder change is about 0.5 percentage points weighted, the same order as the encode margin. Both crates.io releases are yanked.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Encode 1.19-2.36% less time than trunk libopus in all 12 aggregate cells (e.g. 16-bit CBR 192 kb/s: 371.9 ms vs 380.9 ms per 40 s of audio); Rust encoder 96.8-107.6x realtime. The decode lead (1.50-4.64%) is withdrawn by the author's 2026-08-25 same-packet re-test (+0.51% on C packets, -0.30% on Rust packets, +0.10% combined): parity. The encode margin is the same order as the run-to-run drift (about 0.5 percentage points) and the Rust side skips libopus's MLP/GRU analysis classifier.
corrections.caveats: Decode claim invalid (each decoder was timed on its own encoder's packets; same-packet re-test shows parity). Work asymmetry favours Rust: the analysis port skips the MLP/GRU classifier and i16 decode hard-clamps where C soft-clips. The identity checksum covers only packet length plus first and last byte. Both crates.io releases are yanked; successor crate soundkit-opus 0.13.0.

tier_reason: Tier C stands; the complex-script rows are removed from the claim because the library does not do the work: by code reading it ships no Indic, Thai, Khmer, Myanmar or USE default features, its GSUB lookups never read the per-glyph masks set up by the Arabic and Indic code, and the complex-script tests check glyph counts only, so the Hindi 3.6x, Myanmar 10.5x, Thai and Khmer rows compare incomplete shaping against harfbuzzjs's full shaping. The text-to-SVG rows (5.3-7.1x in the committed results) time WeakMap cache hits because pathToSVG is cached while the harfbuzzjs side also pays buffer.json(). shape() ignores buffer direction and the README's bidi auto-reorder claim is not implemented.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Like-for-like rows against harfbuzzjs (committed docs/.vitepress/data/benchmarks.json, ops/s, M1 Pro, Bun 1.3.4, derived from page data): English paragraph 1.48x, Russian/Ukrainian/Belarusian 1.18-1.26x, Greek 1.17x, Chinese/Japanese/Korean 1.26-1.31x, Hebrew 1.24x, Arabic 1.04x. The complex-script rows (Hindi 3.6x, Myanmar 10.5x, Thai 1.58x, Khmer 2.25x) compare incomplete shaping (no Indic, Thai, Khmer, Myanmar or USE default features; GSUB ignores per-glyph masks) against full HarfBuzz shaping; the path-extraction 16x and text-to-SVG 5.3-7.1x rows time WeakMap cache hits. README claims vs opentype.js: 4x to 86x.
